analysis:
Integration of the CI-only PR. It changes the composite action .github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml, ci.yml, component-changes.yml, docs-impact.yml, ci-component-paths.py (new mimo_audio component), install-release-cmake.sh, CI tests and docs. It touches no provider runtime, coordinator protocol, key custody, attestation, App Attest or prefix-cache code, so T-041, TB-002/003/007/009/011/012/013 are unaffected.

Cache poisoning: the replayed action patch confirms a save-caches input (default 'false'). Every save step (Swift build, SwiftPM repos, Metal) is gated on inputs.save-caches == 'true'. The old PR-save path (cache-matched-key == '') is removed. Per the unit analyses, ci.yml sets SAVE_CACHES only for master/dev pushes, so PRs only restore. This reduces the CI cache-poisoning surface. A restored .git is checked only with fsck --connectivity-only and rev-parse; hooks and config are not validated, but only trusted pushes save it and persist-credentials: false keeps the job token out of .git/config.

CMake: install-release-cmake.sh (head) now uses $RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE/cmake/3.31.12/universal when a .complete marker exists and the binary reports 'cmake version 3.31.12'. It skips the sha256 check on this path and falls back to the checksummed download otherwise. This trusts the runner image. Whether release/signing builds use this path, and whether the tool cache is writable by untrusted code, is not in the supplied evidence. I record this as an unverified supply-chain contract, not a finding. The doc says release/signing jobs keep literal Blacksmith labels.

mimo_audio: it is wired through component-changes.yml and ci-component-paths.py (MIMO_AUDIO patterns). Default-branch pushes and COMMON changes still select all components, so the audio gate is a coverage tradeoff for PRs, not a security regression.

Coverage limits: the ci.yml head is only partially seen (jobs after about line 537 were not visible), the replay was incomplete (53 units omitted), and scripts/provider-ci-cache.py was not supplied. A later pass should confirm that the later ci.yml jobs apply the same restore-only policy on PRs, and that release/signing workflows do not restore caches or the tool-cache CMake from untrusted refs.
